dimensions.assessment: Affects all certified pilots and aviation personnel holding airman and medical certificates when inspected by FAA personnel.
dimensions.evidence: An individual issued a certificate pursuant to this section (including a medical certificate) may present such certificate to an inspector of the Federal Aviation Administration

dimensions.assessment: Provides a procedural convenience allowing digital presentation of existing certificates rather than changing underlying certification standards.
dimensions.evidence: A digital certificate issued by the Administrator that is stored on an electronic device or... cloud-based system

dimensions.assessment: No significant federal spending or revenue changes are stated or implied beyond routine administrative rulemaking costs.
Amends title 49 and requires FAA rulemaking updates across parts 61, 63, 65, 67, and 107 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations.
dimensions.evidence: issue a final rule to update regulations in parts 61, 63, 65, 67, and 107 of title 14, Code of Federal Regulations

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory change taking effect after agency rulemaking required by November 2028.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than November 30, 2028, the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall issue a final rule

missing_information: Specific technical specifications for digital certificate verification systems.
importance_detail.rationale: Allows pilots to present digital copies of airman and medical certificates to FAA inspectors, requiring an administrative rulemaking update by late 2028.
